title: Hoi An Ancient Town
summary: Hoi An Ancient Town, on the north bank near the mouth of the Thu Bon River in Quảng Nam Province, is a well-preserved small trading port active from the 15th to the 19th century. Its buildings and street plan blend local and foreign influences, and UNESCO listed it in 1999.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO says the port dates from the 15th to the 19th century; 1401 and 1900 are the first and last years of those centuries. The town still stands and is inscribed on the World Heritage List.

as_recorded.value: a South-East Asian trading port dating from the 15th to the 19th century

where.modern_name: Hội An, Quảng Nam Province, Vietnam
where.historical_name: Hoi An trading port, central coast of Vietnam

importance.justification: A rare surviving small Southeast Asian trading port and a World Heritage property.

sources.title: 25 years of Hoi An as UNESCO World Cultural Heritage Site

reviewer_note: The UNESCO page gives coordinates as N15 52 60 E108 19 60, converted here to decimal degrees. The town is a living place, so the end year is a convention, not a fixed end of the port. The UNESCO page lists a 280-hectare buffer zone that a later UNESCO record corrects, so no area is stated.
